title: The Dead Are Like the Stars by Day
description: The Dead Are Like the Stars by Day in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Bernard Barton wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 353, “The Dead”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The dead are like the stars by day, With-drawn from mor-tal eye, Yet hol-ding un-per-ceived their way Through the un-cloud-ed sky.

lines: The dead are like the stars by day,
By them, through holy hope and love,
For death his sacred seal hath set
And they we mourn are with us yet,
Ours, by the pledge of love and faith,
By hopes of heaven on high;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Bernard Barton died in 1849.
credits: Words by Bernard Barton (1784–1849), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
